firms.name: FTMO
firms.notes: Figures reflect the standard 2-Step Challenge (last directly confirmed at ftmo.com/en/trading-objectives/, Jul 2026; ftmo.com now blocks automated fetches so Aug 2026 re-check relied on secondary sources for pricing/rules — no change reported anywhere, treat as still current). Account/challenge fees are denominated in EUR by default; traders can separately choose a USD/GBP/other trading-account currency, but the challenge cost itself is EUR. Well-established (Czech, founded 2015). NEW: FTMO completed its acquisition of regulated broker OANDA from CVC Capital on 2025-12-01, keeping OANDA as a standalone regulated brokerage with FTMO's founders as co-CEOs alongside OANDA's leadership — a major corporate expansion, not a rebrand or change to FTMO's own (unregulated) challenge product. Not a regulated broker (standard across this industry).

secondaryReview.note: FPA is known for being tougher on prop firms than Trustpilot — a consistent 4.4 there corroborates the Trustpilot number rather than contradicting it.

firms.name: The5%ers
firms.notes: Figures shown are the flat $74/account fee (Pro Growth-style profile, 10%/6%/3%/3-day), scaling to $100k-$125k on performance — last directly confirmed Jul 2026. Aug 2026 re-check: the5ers.com and Trustpilot/FPA now block automated fetches, so this pass relied on secondary sources, which disagree on whether pricing is still a flat $74 or now scales by size (one source describes $74/$140/$270 for $5k/$10k/$20k with no $50k tier under this program) — NOT changed on file pending direct confirmation. The firm now runs several concurrent programs (Bootcamp, Pro Growth, High Stakes, Hyper Growth) that may have different payout splits/frequencies than shown; treat the single profile here as approximate. No rebrand found (a brief Feb 2024 pause on new US traders was resolved by 2025). Documented complaints of payout denials and account terminations citing vague 'integrity concerns' shortly after profitable trades, with unresponsive support in several reported cases. IMPORTANT: ForexPeaceArmy's paid/fake review campaign finding (zero-star rating) remains unresolved as of Aug 2026 — treat its very high Trustpilot score with real caution. Also flagged unregulated by WikiFX with a Central Bank of Russia warning note.

externalReview.note: Review-count figures vary widely by source (17k-34k as of Aug 2026); treated as approximate. See manipulation warning below — this score should not be taken at face value.

firms.name: FundedNext
firms.notes: Runs several challenge types (Stellar, Rapid, Legacy, Bolt) with different rules — figures shown are the Stellar 1-Step (last directly confirmed via help.fundednext.com, Jul 2026; the site remains JS-rendered/blocked to automated fetches, so Aug 2026 figures are secondary-source corroborated, not primary-verified). A March 2025 'FN' rebrand was cosmetic only (new logo/vision statement, no name or ownership change). On 2026-07-10 the futures-side Bolt and Rapid Futures challenges were retired for new purchases (replaced by Rapid Pro/Rapid Daily/Flex Challenge; existing Bolt accounts grandfathered) — the CFD Stellar lineup shown here is unaffected. Some secondary sources now cite higher Stellar pricing (~$130/$220/$330/$570/$1,100) and a shorter min-days/faster payout cadence than shown below, but this could not be confirmed against fundednext.com directly this cycle — treat current figures as pending re-verification, not as confirmed unchanged. EA/algo trading is allowed on Stellar forex/CFD accounts, with a separate EA usage fee, a requirement to customize/de-duplicate strategy settings (identical copy-trading across accounts is banned), a $300k max allocation per single EA/strategy, and no EA support on cTrader. Base (non-promo) Stellar pricing shown — promo codes offering ~30% off the challenge fee are commonly available at checkout. No rebrand of the entity found. Documented complaints include retroactively rejected refunds (including a specific 2026 crypto-refund dispute feeding an active Dubai consumer-authority complaint) and an under-disclosed 3.5% payout processing fee. IMPORTANT: ForexPeaceArmy's Jan 2024 finding of fraudulent 5-star reviews traced to the same IP as FundedNext's own Bangladesh Partner Manager remains unretracted as of Aug 2026 — a confirmed instance of review manipulation, not just a suspicion.

externalReview.note: Sources vary 62k-75k reviews; treated as approximate. See manipulation warning below — some of this firm's positive review volume has been directly traced to fake accounts.

secondaryReview.note: No clean aggregate score — FPA's review thread documents fake 5-star reviews traced to FundedNext's own Partner Manager IP address.

firms.name: Apex Trader Funding
firms.notes: AVAILABILITY: secondary sources (Apr 2026 restricted-country lists) say Apex does not allow South African residents to open accounts, request payouts or use the platform. Not confirmed against apextraderfunding.com, which blocks automated access. PRICING NOT CURRENT: the accounts[] costs and 'monthly' wording below are the pre-March-2026 monthly-subscription rates. Apex 4.0 moved to a one-time evaluation fee; current per-tier prices could not be verified from apextraderfunding.com (blocks automated access, 403, as of 2026-10-05), so no new figures were guessed. Futures focused — indices only. IMPORTANT UPDATE (Aug 2026): apextraderfunding.com continues to return 403 to automated fetches, and this cycle so did essentially every third-party review/aggregator site tested — findings below are WebSearch-snippet synthesis only, not primary-verified, and are lower-confidence than usual. Multiple independent secondary sources agree that a structural overhaul called 'Apex 4.0' launched 2026-03-01, replacing the old recurring MONTHLY subscription evaluation model with a ONE-TIME evaluation fee, introducing two drawdown types (Intraday Trailing vs. End-of-Day), and removing the old MAE rule, 5:1 R/R rule, and 7-day minimum-trading-day rule; pre-4.0 monthly-subscription accounts are now legacy/no-longer-sold. The figures below (monthly-rate approximations, 7-day min days) reflect the PRE-4.0 model still on file from last cycle and are now stale — exact current one-time per-tier pricing could not be confirmed against a primary source this cycle (secondary sources suggest roughly $199/$249/$399/$599 one-time for the $25k/$50k/$100k/$150k Intraday tiers, no figure found for $300k), so left unchanged here pending direct re-verification rather than guessed. Same top-tier complaint volume as before: an $800k dispute between two traders, AG complaints filed in Michigan and Texas, and an active gag-order lawsuit against a YouTuber over bait-and-switch claims — PLUS a NEW federal suit, Lawton v. Apex Trader Funding Inc. et al (W.D. Tex., 1:26-cv-02078, filed 2026-07-24), alleging fraudulent/deceptive practices and undisclosed risk; Apex denies the allegations and the case is pending. Despite the 4.0 overhaul being marketed around 'no more payout denials,' traders continue to report denials and account freezes post-payout. A March 2026 metals-trading suspension (GC, SI, MGC, HG, PL, PA, QI, QO) remains in effect with no announced return date.

externalReview.note: Trustpilot skews positive because reviews are often left right after funding, before payout disputes surface — see our complaint research in the notes above. About 8.7% of Trustpilot reviews are 1-star, describing slow payouts, account closures after becoming profitable, and support going silent.

secondaryReview.note: FPA's review thread contains detailed trader complaints about payout restrictions and rule enforcement — consistent with our own lawsuit/complaint findings above despite the decent aggregate Trustpilot number.

firms.name: E8 Markets (E8 Funding)
firms.notes: Rebranded from E8 Funding to E8 Markets in Nov 2023 (e8funding.com now 301-redirects here), alongside a Riseworks payout integration and clearer consistency-rule documentation. Highly customizable at checkout: drawdown up to 14% (raises target to 21%), daily loss up to 9.2%, payout up to 100%. Now spans four product lines (E8 One, E8 Pro, E8 Signature, and a new E8 Zero one-phase 6%/3% challenge launched 2026-07-06) with rules that vary by product — figures shown are the E8 One default profile. News trading: the funded E8 One stage applies a 5-minute blackout around Tier 1 news (flagged false here for that reason); E8 Zero, Signature and Pro allow news trading in challenge and performance. Weekend holding is allowed on E8 One but E8 Signature (Forex/Crypto) force-closes positions daily at 23:00 server time — figures shown reflect E8 One. Pre-rebrand history included a public $500k payout dispute and after-the-fact rule additions; no new lawsuits, regulatory actions, or payout disputes found since the rebrand — complaint volume remains reported as notably cleaner, with recent negative reviews focused on rule complexity and funded-account processing wait times rather than withheld payouts. e8markets.com and most review sites blocked automated fetches this cycle (403), so pricing/rule figures are secondary-source corroborated rather than primary-confirmed.

secondaryReview.note: Generally positive on FPA too — fast payouts and responsive support are recurring themes, though some traders report rules (like leverage) changing immediately after passing a challenge.

firms.name: Topstep
firms.notes: Futures focused — indices only. IMPORTANT: the Trading Combine is a recurring MONTHLY subscription, not a one-time fee — figures below are confirmed unchanged current monthly rates ($49/$99/$199 + a $149 one-time activation fee on funding). A real 50%-best-day consistency rule exists — a single day's profit above 50% of the profit target blocks passing until diluted by more trading days; a day only counts toward progress at all if net profit clears $150. There's no separate hard minimum-day count — minDays=10 is an approximation of how many winning days most passes actually need to satisfy the consistency rule, not a stated rule itself. Max drawdown varies by tier in dollar terms ($2,000/$50k=4%, $3,000/$100k=3%, $4,500/$150k=3%) — figure shown (3%) reflects the more commonly funded $100k/$150k tiers. EA/algo trading is allowed during the Combine evaluation but funded 'Live' TopstepX accounts prohibit fully automated EAs/bots/trade copiers. As of 2026-01-12 new accounts get a flat 90/10 payout split from the first dollar (previously 100% of the first $10k, then 90/10 — older accounts remain grandfathered). No rebrand (Topstep acquired competitor 'The Futures Desk' in Apr 2026 and consolidated onto its own TopstepX platform); it newly registered with the NFA as a member/Swap Firm/CTA around May 2026, apparently in response to the lawsuit's unregistered-CPO claim. Still named in an active federal lawsuit (McCrudden v. Topstep, M.D. Fla. 3:26-cv-00816, filed 2026-04-09, pro se) alleging a 'systematic and deceptive scheme' of shifting rules and inaccessible profit reserves — no dismissal or settlement found as of this check. Topstep also confirmed 11 TopstepX platform outages Oct-Dec 2025 that caused forced liquidations, and BBB complaints roughly tripled over the same period; a prior 2022 lawsuit (Footlick v. Topstep) was dismissed with prejudice by stipulation in 2024. Topstep has also pursued legal action against at least one public critic, resulting in a speaking ban.

externalReview.note: Down from 3.5 ("Average") last cycle — the lowest Trustpilot score of any active firm in this comparison, consistent with the 2025 outages, tripled BBB complaints, and active lawsuit above.

firms.name: True Forex Funds

firms.name: Blue Guardian
firms.notes: Base (non-promo) pricing shown — the site frequently runs 30-60% off launch codes at checkout. Profit target is 8% (Phase 1) / 4% (Phase 2), max drawdown 8% and daily loss 4% confirmed unchanged via help.blueguardian.com. UPDATED: default funded profit split is now 85% (was 90%) — 90% is offered only as a paid checkout add-on (per help.blueguardian.com's '7-day payout and 90% profit split add-on' article). UPDATED: news trading is no longer a blanket ban — for accounts purchased after 2025-11-13, opening/closing trades within 5 minutes before or after high-impact ('red folder') news (incl. FOMC) is prohibited on funded accounts, but news trading outside that window or during the challenge phase is allowed. In 2024 the firm acquired an ASIC-licensed broker and rebranded it 'Guardian Markets' for non-US clients (a separate entity from the core prop-firm product) — confusingly, Trustpilot now displays the business name 'Guardian Markets' for the blueguardian.com listing. Owned by Iconic Exchange FZCO (Dubai), founded 2021, no rebrand of the core prop-firm product found. Documented complaints include the 'Guardian Shield' mechanism auto-closing trades on ~1-2% floating loss, stop-losses reportedly being ignored then blamed on the trader, payout denials even after prior successful payouts, an Apr 2026 FPA thread alleging software was used to trigger account breaches and deny payouts, silently changed daily-loss enforcement from soft to hard breach without notice, and vague 'shared device'/'ban evasion' terminations.

externalReview.note: Ratings vary unusually widely by platform (3.6 here vs 4.1-4.8 reported elsewhere) — treat any single number with caution. Trustpilot now displays this listing under the business name "Guardian Markets" (see notes above).

secondaryReview.note: Contains a detailed complaint from a profitable trader whose account was breached and access refused even after support acknowledged unauthorized activity, plus an Apr 2026 thread alleging software-triggered breaches — worth reading before purchasing.

firms.name: Fidelcrest
firms.notes: CONFIRMED SHUT DOWN as an apparent exit scam in March 2024 — the firm continued accepting challenge payments while unable to deliver service, refused refunds to traders in good standing, then ceased all communication. Re-checked Aug 2026: fidelcrest.com again returned 403 to automated fetches, so current on-site content (previously described as unrelated third-party content) could not be re-confirmed this cycle, but multiple independent sources (Trustpilot, shutdown trackers, scam-tracking sites) continue to describe it as shut down with no relaunch, successor brand, asset sale, or trader repayment found. Some SEO 'review 2026' pages still describe it as active — treat those as stale/unverified, not evidence. Do not republish as active or recommend under any circumstances.

firms.name: City Traders Imperium
firms.notes: EA/algo is allowed only with proof of source-code ownership — third-party/black-box bots and automated news-scalping are prohibited. Payouts: first payout on-demand after 7 profitable days + 2% profit, then monthly for 1-Step/2-Step (bi-weekly for Instant Funding); payout split shown (70%) is the starting point and reportedly scales up toward 100% with a longer funded track record. No rebrand found; publicly contrasted its own stability against the 2024-2026 prop-firm shutdown wave (e.g. MyForexFunds' collapse). Operating since 2018 — 21,000+ funded traders and $367M+ paid out per last check (some 2026 secondary sources cite ~36,000+ funded traders, unconfirmed against the primary site this cycle). Aug 2026 re-check: citytradersimperium.com and Trustpilot/FPA blocked automated fetches, so this pass relied on secondary sources, which show some internal disagreement on exact current pricing, min trading days, and whether news/weekend-holding rules have loosened — left unchanged here pending direct re-verification; one aggregator also cites a possible new $5k account tier not reflected below. No new lawsuits or regulatory actions found. Some standard-pattern complaints about payout denials tied to copy-trading/high-risk rule enforcement, but no indication of scam behavior.

secondaryReview.note: Only 2 reviews on FPA — too small a sample to mean much on its own, shown mainly because it doesn't contradict the Trustpilot picture.

firms.name: Lux Trading Firm
firms.notes: GBP-priced, not EUR/USD as previously listed — account tiers below are the real 1-Step Evaluation sizes (£199/£449/£999), re-confirmed directly from luxtradingfirm.com content Aug 2026. Similarly, one aggregator claims cross-account copy trading is prohibited (vs. copyTrading:true shown here) and that only self-developed EAs are allowed (third-party/HFT/arbitrage EAs prohibited) — also unconfirmed, left unchanged. Confirmed NOT the same company as 'Lucid Trading' or 'Luxemarkets' — distinct, unrelated firms that sometimes get confused with it in reviews, no rebrand. Still operates without an FCA/ASIC or other financial regulator license; independent reviews continue to report very few confirmed trader payout stories, recurring withdrawal-delay/technical-difficulty complaints, and disputes where the firm attributes errors to 'database/server failures' with no compensation offered. No new lawsuits or regulatory actions found.

externalReview.note: Review counts reported elsewhere range from ~400 to ~650 — low enough volume that this figure moves a lot per new review, unlike the larger firms in this list.

secondaryReview.note: Only 1 review on FPA (2 stars) — not enough data to draw a conclusion from, but it doesn't support the Trustpilot picture either.

firms.name: MyForexFunds
firms.notes: UPDATED Aug 2026: the CFTC's case against parent Traders Global Group was dismissed WITH PREJUDICE on 2025-05-13 (a Special Master found the CFTC had misled the court; the CFTC itself was sanctioned) — a materially favorable legal development from the original 2023 CFTC/SEC fraud allegations. The Ontario Superior Court receivership was correspondingly scaled back, with a final Canadian asset-return order in Dec 2025. A Feb 2026 announcement committed to honoring verified Aug-2023 payout claims, with some payouts reportedly issued by May 2026, but as of the most recent reporting (Apr-Jul 2026) the company itself says it is still conducting a full financial/operational/technical review before any relaunch decision — this remains a recovery/repayment phase, not normal operations, and it is not accepting new challenge purchases as a going concern. One low-quality aggregator (start-business-online.com) claimed a new 'Unlimited Days' evaluation product launched 2026-07-17 implying active sales, but this is uncorroborated by any credible outlet (Finance Magnates, PR Newswire, etc.) and is treated as unverified, consistent with this site's policy of discounting unsourced aggregator claims. Re-verify before ever setting active:true — specifically watch for credible confirmation (or denial) of the 'Unlimited Days' relaunch claim.
